node.title: L1 official first-checkpoint split-pencil reduction
node.statement: On an official multiplicative-coset domain, let p<=d<=2p-2 and suppose a minimum-width coarse p-free collision has disjoint tails of size t=p. The tail locators must differ by a nonzero constant and have the exact form F_X=Z^p+Q+b, F_Y=Z^p+Q+b+c with deg Q<=r_d=2p-d-1. Conversely every disjoint fully split pair of this form gives the required moment collision. On the nonzero one of the two fibers, every nonidentity multiplicative ratio has at most r_d witnesses, so its ratio set has size at least 1+ceil((p^2-p)/r_d). Hence no t=p collision exists when r_d<=r_*(p,n)=floor((p(p-1)-1)/(n-1)), equivalently d>=2p-1-r_*(p,n). The official inequality 11n<=256p gives the uniform floor r_*>=floor(11(p-1)/256). The terminal affine-line case is an independent structural check. The surviving lower-depth object is a typed higher-degree split-pencil census, not a proved row-sharp bound.
